overview: From 2026-08-27 to 2026-08-28, ethereum-optimism/ecosystem had 2 new PRs (0 merged), 1 new issues, and 5 active contributors.

topIssues.title: SuperchainERC20 compatibility checking has no home
topIssues.author: jefr90
topIssues.body:
Split out of #1017, which archives `ethereum-optimism/superchainerc20-compatibility`. Logging the capability so it is not lost with the repo.

**The gap:** there is no supported way for a developer to point at a token address and find out whether it is a valid, interop-compatible SuperchainERC20.

`superchainerc20-compatibility` was an unfinished attempt at exactly this: a `packages/checks` library (ERC-7802 interface support, crosschain mint/burn permissions, crosschain mint/burn event emission, contract deployment) plus a `packages/checker-ui` React front end that ran them across chains. Four commits, all Nov/Dec 2024, never finished or announced.

**Why it may still matter:** this overlaps with #1016, which notes there is no registration path for SuperchainERC20 tokens. A compatibility checker and a token registry are the same problem viewed from two ends, and neither currently exists.

**What has changed since it was written:** the checks target `SuperchainTokenBridge`, deleted from the OP Stack in [optimism#19999](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19999) (released in `op-node/v1.16.13`). The mint/burn permission checks are therefore obsolete as written. The ERC-7802 interface check remains valid. Reviving this means rewriting roughly half of it against the current interop contracts, not restoring the archived repo.

**Asks:**

- Decide whether the capability is still wanted.
- If yes, decide where it belongs: a package in the ecosystem repo, part of whatever #1016 concludes about the token registry, or a docs-only guide showing developers how to check by hand.
- If no, close this and let the archive stand.

topPRs.title: docs: state the supported surface in the README
topPRs.author: jefr90
topPRs.body:
Closes #1011. Part of the #1008 interop public repo cleanup.

**Stacked on #1018** (the relayer removal), so the README is written once against the post-removal tree. Base is `julio/1010-remove-superseded-relayer`; retarget to `main` once that merges.

## What

Rewrites the repo intro to answer the question a developer actually has when they land here: which of this is supported?

- **What this repo is / is not** sections, leading with `packages/viem` and `packages/wagmi`.
- A table classifying **every** app and package as Supported or Experimental. Nothing is left unlabelled: the table covers all 7 directories under `apps/` and `packages/`.
- A section stating what the starter kits depend on.
- Drops the old intro line that linked "the Optimism Repository" to `ethereum-optimism/ecosystem`, i.e. to itself, where it meant the monorepo.

## Classification and the evidence behind it

npm downloads, last month:

| Package | Downloads/mo | Latest | Published | Classified |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `@eth-optimism/viem` | 6,554 | 0.4.15 | 2026-04-16 | Supported |
| `@eth-optimism/utils-app` | 4,050 | 0.0.6 | 2025-05-27 | Supported |
| `@eth-optimism/ponder-interop` | 2,210 | 0.0.24 | 2026-04-17 | Experimental |
| `supersim` | 295 | 0.1.0-alpha.59 | 2025-08-06 | Supported |
| `@eth-optimism/wagmi` | 287 | 0.1.14 | 2026-04-16 | Supported |

Two calls worth a second opinion:

- **`utils-app` has 14x the downloads of `wagmi`** despite never being called out anywhere. I marked it Supported on that basis, but it is a lifecycle helper rather than a developer-facing interop library, so "Supported" may be overstating the commitment.
- **`ponder-interop` is Experimental despite 2,210 downloads/month.** It is a reference indexer, and `sponsored-sender` (its usual companion) says in its own README that it is not for production. If ponder-interop is in fact something we support, say so and I will move it.

`sponsored-sender` and `superchain-playground` are `"private": true`, so they have no npm signal and are Experimental by construction.

## One finding that lands on a different issue

I verified the starter-kit dependency claim rather than asserting it, by grepping the six cloned starter repos. Result:

- All six declare **`@eth-optimism/viem`**. None declare `@eth-optimism/wagmi`.
- Five of the six also declare **`@eth-optimism/super-cli`**: `superchain-starter`, `superchain-starter-superchainerc20`, `superchain-starter-xchain-flash-loan-example`, `superchain-starter-xchain-eth-multitransfer`, `superchain-starter-pingpong`.

That second point matters for [ecosystem#1012](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/1012), which proposes deprecating `super-cli` on the grounds of low adoption. It is a declared dependency of five starter repos, so deprecating it is not free. I have recorded this against that issue's decision rather than acting on it here.

## Verification

`for d in apps/* packages/*; do grep -q "(\./$d)" README.md; done` passes for all 7 directories, so the table cannot silently drop one.

topPRs.title: chore: remove superseded autorelayer-interop app
topPRs.author: jefr90
topPRs.body:
Closes #1010. Part of the #1008 interop public repo cleanup.

## What

Removes `apps/autorelayer-interop`, its Docker build stage, its `.github/images.json` entry, and its lockfile importer. Also fixes a pre-existing CI break (last section).

The lockfile change is a surgical 20-line removal of the importer block, not a regeneration: a plain `pnpm install --lockfile-only` also pulled in unrelated drift (viem 2.33.0, `@types/node` churn) that does not belong here.

## The successor has been confirmed

The issue's premise holds. The relayer is actively maintained in a **separate, private** repository, where it has grown well beyond the copy being deleted here:

| | this repo (deleted) | successor |
|---|---|---|
| `src/` layout | `api`, `config`, `schemas`, `types`, `utils`, `relayer.ts` | `admin`, `deposit`, `metrics`, `relay`, `services`, `strategies`, `relayer.ts`, plus `__tests__` and a vitest config |
| last functional change | 2025-07-15 | **2026-08-13** ("registry correctness, module defaults, and budgeting"), after "Reintegrate promise + callback relaying" on 2026-07-14 |

So this removal is correct, and the code here is genuinely superseded.

**One open question before merge:** the successor repo is private, so the README cannot usefully link it for external developers. It currently says the relayer moved and has no public home yet, without naming the repo. Naming a private repo in a public README discloses its existence, which felt like a call for you rather than me. Tell me which you want:

1. Leave it as is (moved, no public home).
2. Name the private repo explicitly.
3. Different wording you prefer.

## What I kept, and why

`ponder-interop` and `sponsored-sender` stay. The issue says to remove "anything related", but neither is a relayer dependency in the direction that matters: both are standalone deployables with their own Docker images and build targets, and neither imports the autorelayer. Only the autorelayer imported them. `apps/ponder-interop/README.md` had the sole prose cross-reference; its dangling relative link is fixed.

## The npm package is live

`@eth-optimism/autorelayer-interop` had **2,345 downloads in the last month**, latest `0.0.26` published 2026-04-17. For scale, `@eth-optimism/wagmi` gets 287/month. Deleting the source without deprecating the package leaves installers with no signal. I have not run `npm deprecate`, since that is outward-facing. Suggested at merge:

```
npm deprecate @eth-optimism/autorelayer-interop "Superseded; this app has been removed from ethereum-optimism/ecosystem"
```

The published Docker image `ecosystem-autorelayer-interop` also stops being built by this PR.

## History

Reachable at [`62d792fe`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/tree/62d792fe05b73c4d0ceb1f99fb75c919eb634d64/apps/autorelayer-interop), which the README links. If you want a durable tag too, push `archive/autorelayer-interop` at merge; I did not push one unilaterally.

## Included CI fix (pre-existing, unrelated to the removal)

Image builds were failing on `apk add --no-cache python3=3.12.13-r0 …` with "unable to select packages". Alpine drops superseded patch builds, and `alpine3.21` now ships `3.12.14-r0`. This is a line the removal never touched, and it failed for `ponder-interop` and `sponsored-sender`, two images whose inputs are unchanged here.

Pinning the patch guarantees recurrence on every Alpine bump, so python3 is now pinned to the minor (`=~3.12`). `make` and `g++` stay exact.

## Verification

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passes, so the surgical lockfile edit is consistent
- `pnpm nx run-many -t build,typecheck --all` green across all 6 projects
- `pnpm nx run-many -t lint --all` green across all 7 projects
- Both Docker targets build locally, and all 17 CI checks pass
- `grep -ri autorelayer` returns only the intentional README note and a historical `packages/utils-app/CHANGELOG.md` entry, left alone deliberately
